supporting_information.scope: All supplied SI figures through S39 and source numerical listings; no current QD coordinates or raw curve files.

independent_audit: All eight supplied main pages and 25 matched SI pages read and independently audited. Canonical records, corrected reader, molecular references and bindings, stage-specific apparatus and symbolic product contexts passed separate audits. Four conversion route/variant records, fifteen supporting procedures and eleven observation records retain their separate contexts. Source inconsistencies and unreported conditions remain explicit. No current-product atomic coordinates, exact structure–recipe pair or new training task is admitted.
publication_status: Published after independent source, canonical, illustration and integrated browser reviews; exact deployed GitHub Pages commit and anonymous public bytes verified. Complete supplied main and matched SI reviewed; source conflicts remain explicit.

items.title: Cluster precursors, additives and isotope-labeled ligands
items.text: Preformed InP magic-size clusters are the conversion precursors. Myristate, phenylacetate and carbonyl-13C phenylacetate contexts remain separate. The article supplies a full labeled-phenylacetic-acid preparation, while cluster, labeled indium-carboxylate and phosphorus-precursor preparations are cited or incomplete. Stock concentrations, isotope enrichment and reaction transfers retain their own source scopes.

items.title: Local structure, diffraction and domain-size analysis
items.text: TEM, local Fourier transforms and powder diffraction support source phase and morphology assignments. The 250 °C TEM specimen is described as spherical particles with a 2.6 ± 0.5 nm mean diameter from 315 particles. InP and In2O3 assignments and separated fractions do not establish pure whole-product composition. Source-calculated Scherrer domains, including conflicting fit-box and prose values, are distinct from microscopy diameters. No current QD atomic coordinates are supplied.

items.title: Optical, magnetic-resonance and thermal observations
items.text: Temperature, concentration and carboxylate perturbations are followed through optical spectra, NMR and thermal analysis. The 500 nm response and its fitted slope are optical proxies, not calibrated isolated yields. Published Gaussian maxima, kinetic regressions and thermal annotations remain literal source evidence with their original units and conflicts. Separate contexts do not establish the same physical aliquot across techniques.

items.title: Reversible ligand dynamics
items.text: Variable-temperature 13C NMR in toluene-d8 shows a crowded carbonyl region and coalescence at 80 °C that reverses upon returning to room temperature. Text cooling is −35 °C while Figure 1 labels −30 °C. Assignment to ligand exchange is an author interpretation, not a measured atomistic trajectory.

items.title: Low-temperature pretreatment
items.text: Heating at 130 °C for 30 h reduces the sharp cluster absorption and gives broad 31P resonances with new phosphorus environments. Figure 4B compares conversion of these two samples at 250 °C. Elsewhere the same discussion and SI 15/16 specify 72 h pretreatment, so a unique 30/72 h cross-panel join is unresolved.

items.title: Optical evolution, diffraction and TEM
items.text: Optical evolution, diffraction and TEM. Panel A shows spectra at 250 °C after 0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 and 60 min, with an inset at 500, 600 and 700 nm. Panel B compares the 500 nm response at 150, 200, 250 and 300 °C; panel C compares final absorption at those temperatures. Panel D compares 150 and 250 °C XRD patterns with InP and In2O3 references. Panel E shows 150 °C agglomerates and panel F shows 250 °C spherical particles; both TEM panels have 20 nm scale bars. Panel F reports 2.6 ± 0.5 nm from 315 particles; the definition of the ± uncertainty is not specified.

items.title: Proposed ligand exchange and cluster dissolution
items.text: The authors discuss ligand rearrangement, carboxylate-promoted dissolution and competing productive and nonproductive channels. These mechanisms and the Scheme 1 stoichiometric relation are interpretations. Cited earlier cluster structures and theoretical calculations remain attributed context; no new elementary-reaction product counts, DFT model or molecular coordinates are inferred.

items.title: Prior cluster preparation and structure
items.text: Earlier work isolated a 386 nm absorbing intermediate at 100 °C. The previously determined phenylacetate cluster is In37P20(O2CCH2Ph)51; its [In21P20]3+ core, 16 surface indium atoms and 51 predominantly bridging bidentate carboxylates are cited structural context, not coordinates newly supplied here.

items.title: Additive effects and competing interpretation
items.text: At 50 equivalents, acid growth is approximately half the indium-myristate growth rate. At 150 °C, additives strongly affect the final optical distribution but weakly affect growth rate; at 250 °C and above, product absorption distributions change little. Carboxylate-mediated dissolution, acid activation and monomer stabilization are proposed alternatives.

items.title: Background mechanisms and prior systems
items.text: The introduction contrasts monomer deposition on seeds, quantized growth/Ostwald staging, full dissolution/renucleation and cluster assembly/oriented attachment. CdSe, CdTe, ZnTe, ZnS, PbS, PbSe, Ag2S, ZnO and metal-nanoparticle studies are cited as comparisons; their syntheses and structures are not current InP sample records. In situ UV–vis, scattering and liquid-cell microscopy examples establish methodological context.

figures.label: Variable-temperature 13C NMR and absorption
figures.caption_paraphrase: Variable-temperature 13C NMR and absorption. Panel A shows 13C NMR in toluene-d8 at 176 MHz, with labels −30, 25 and 80 °C and return to 25 °C. Panel B shows absorption from 20 to 110 °C in 10 °C steps; its caption identifies phenylacetate MSCs in toluene. Conflicting prose temperature endpoints remain explicit elsewhere.

figures.label: Labeled acid and indium-carboxylate exchange
figures.caption_paraphrase: Labeled acid and indium-carboxylate exchange. Panel A compares natural-abundance MSCs with 1, 10 or 30 equivalents of 13C-labeled acid, alongside authentic labeled MSC and free-acid references. Panel B compares 1, 5, 10 or 20 equivalents of labeled indium salt and an authentic labeled-MSC reference; the caption specifies toluene-d8 and 176 MHz.

figures.label: Optical evolution, diffraction and TEM
figures.caption_paraphrase: Optical evolution, diffraction and TEM. Panel A shows spectra at 250 °C after 0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 and 60 min, with an inset at 500, 600 and 700 nm. Panel B compares the 500 nm response at 150, 200, 250 and 300 °C; panel C compares final absorption at those temperatures. Panel D compares 150 and 250 °C XRD patterns with InP and In2O3 references. Panel E shows 150 °C agglomerates and panel F shows 250 °C spherical particles; both TEM panels have 20 nm scale bars. Panel F reports 2.6 ± 0.5 nm from 315 particles; the definition of the ± uncertainty is not specified.

figures.label: Pretreatment NMR and conversion comparison
figures.caption_paraphrase: Pretreatment NMR and conversion comparison. Panel A shows 31P NMR in C6D6 after pretreatment at 130 °C for 30 h and literally prints 202 Hz. Panel B follows conversion at 250 °C through the 500 nm response. The 30 h/72 h pretreatment descriptions do not establish an exact cross-panel specimen match.

remaining_gaps: Full natural/myristate MSC, labeled indium phenylacetate, P(SiMe3)3 and indium-myristate reference preparations are not supplied. Labeled MSC only replaces acid in cited references 43 and 45. Prior crystal coordinates are not attached.
Concentrations, aliquot volumes, equilibration times and exact ligand-exchange rates are unreported for NMR titrations. No dissolved species geometry is determined.

Many solvent amounts, vacuum pressure, stirring speed, ramps, drying settings and numerical room temperature are not given. Thermal analysis atmosphere is unreported; source reaction nitrogen is not inherited.
Representative charge does not prove identical preparation for every plotted condition. GPC details/isolated QD yield and exact cross-technique physical batch joins are absent.

Curves are supplied as figures, not raw datasets. No curve digitization/refit was performed. Complete Scherrer implementation, errors and instrumental broadening treatment are absent. All reported fit coefficients remain source calculations.

No supplied atomic-coordinate/CIF model for current clusters or QDs, no sample-exact crystal structure, no measured DFT pairing; training eligibility stays false. FFT microscopy evidence is not mislabeled SAED.
